key_structures: East-facing Meenakshi Amman and Sundareswarar shrines in separate nested prakaras
Four nine-tier Raja Gopurams, smaller precinct towers and two gilded sanctuary vimanas
Ayiram Kaal Mandapam (Thousand Pillar Hall) in the northeastern compound
Potramarai Kulam (Golden Lily Tank) east of Meenakshi with four colonnades
Ashta Shakti, Veda, Meenakshi Nayaka and Chitra Gopuram on the east approach
Kambathadi Mandapa, Velli Ambalam and Kalyana Mandapa
special_features: Meenakshi’s two-armed standing form with lotus and parrot
Mukkuruni Vinayagar and Velli Ambalam’s right-leg-raised Nataraja
Eight named Ashta Shakti stone figures with their documented north and south order
Musical pillar designs and selected documented relief subjects at Ayiram Kaal
Nayak-period mural locations and temple inscriptions recorded in the heritage sources
materials: Fine stucco and lime plaster for thousands of gopuram sculptures
renovation_history: Pandyas established the ancient shrine; after 14th-century disruptions, magnificently rebuilt and expanded to present cosmic layout by Nayaka dynasty rulers, especially Thirumalai Nayak.
